title: Modelling the options embedded in a German Bauspar contract
summary: An open project, stated as an intention and not yet worked: to model the options a German building-society savings contract contains. It sits between the workshop's rational-exercise treatment of §489 and the behavioural evidence that borrowers do not follow that rule.
friction: Review of the first draft surfaced the obstacle that decides whether this project is tractable: a hazard fitted to observed borrower behaviour is a real-world probability, while the swaption valuation is risk-neutral. Substituting the first into the second is not automatic, and no correction has been chosen.

The first framing treated behavioural deviation as replacing the rational-exercise rule. That was too strong. §489 is the borrower's right, so failure to exercise costs the lender less; optimal exercise is the conservative bound and the threshold survives as the main explanatory variable of exercise intensity rather than as the exercise law.
notes: The exported project carries a description and no documents. Recorded because an empty project with a clear question is a real position in the corpus, and because it names the gap the Efron bridge proposes to fill. No evidence and no friction: nothing has been done yet, and the record must not suggest otherwise. Friction here comes from review of the draft post rather than from building the model; the record says so rather than implying work that has not happened.
